items.name: FCA Guidance on AI/ML
items.description: Financial Policy Note 04/2024: AI/ML guidance for financial services

requirements.text: Firms should have clear accountability for AI system governance, with senior management oversight.
requirements.rationale: Senior oversight ensures AI systems align with firm-wide risk appetite.

controls.description: Appoint a named senior manager responsible for AI governance with clear charter and board reporting obligations.

requirements.text: AI systems should be subject to the same risk management standards as any other system used by the firm.
requirements.rationale: AI systems pose similar operational risks to other critical systems.

controls.description: Apply the firm's existing risk management framework (ERM, operational risk, third-party risk) to AI systems without exception.

requirements.text: Firms using AI should ensure data quality, provenance, and lineage are well-documented.
requirements.rationale: Poor data quality leads to biased or unreliable AI outputs.

controls.description: Document data provenance for all AI training and operational data; verify data quality metrics at intake and at regular intervals.

requirements.text: Firms should test for bias in AI systems and take remedial action where bias is identified.
requirements.rationale: Bias testing is essential for regulatory compliance and ethical AI use.

controls.description: Implement automated bias detection tests across protected characteristics; schedule quarterly re-testing; document remediation actions.

requirements.text: AI-driven decisions should not produce outcomes that breach the Consumer Duty.
requirements.rationale: AI systems must deliver good outcomes for retail customers.

controls.description: Conduct Consumer Duty impact assessments for all AI systems serving retail customers; monitor outcomes post-deployment.
